module_name_en: Core Words III and Graded Reading

learn.explanation_en: उम्मीद covers both hope and expectation, which English keeps apart. मुझे उम्मीद है कि वह आएगा is "I hope he'll come" and also "I expect he'll come", and Hindi does not force you to choose. It is feminine and it ends in a consonant, so nothing about its shape tells you that — this is one to flag. The related आशा is the Sanskrit-side word and belongs to more formal writing; उम्मीद is what people say.

examples.hindi: मुझे उम्मीद है कि वह आएगा।
examples.read_as: mujhe ummiid hai ki vah aaegaa.
examples.note: The dative experiencer from Module 10 — hope arrives at you.
मत for an instruction, from Module 12.
The plural is उम्मीदें, and the adjective goes feminine plural with it.

common_error.why_en: उम्मीद is feminine despite the consonant ending, so the possessive is मेरी.

practice.explanation_en: One word covering both hope and expectation.

game.question_en: Which word would a formal written report use instead of उम्मीद?
game.explanation_en: आशा is the Sanskrit-side equivalent and belongs to formal writing. भरोसा is trust, not hope, and इच्छा is a wish.

tts_strings: मुझे उम्मीद है कि वह आएगा।

learn.explanation_en: कोशिश is an attempt, and it lives almost entirely inside कोशिश करना, to try. Hindi has no single verb for "try" — you make an attempt. That means the noun carries the gender and the करना half carries everything else: मैंने कोशिश की, with की feminine because कोशिश is. कोशिश is feminine and consonant-final, so flag it — nothing in the word predicts the gender. This is the same shape as मदद की and बात की, and it is one of the commonest patterns in the language.

examples.note: ने because करना is transitive, and की because कोशिश is feminine.
The रहना construction for continuing, from Module 12.

examples.hindi: एक बार और कोशिश कर लो।
examples.read_as: ek baar aur koshish kar lo.
examples.note: The लेना vector — do it for your own sake.

common_error.why_en: कोशिश is feminine, so करना agrees with it.

practice.explanation_en: Literally to make an attempt. Hindi has no single verb for "try".

game.question_en: Which of these is closest to कोशिश in an official notice?
game.explanation_en: प्रयास is the formal register equivalent. इरादा is an intention rather than an attempt, and मेहनत is hard work rather than a try.

learn.explanation_en: ज़रूरत is a need, and मुझे ज़रूरत है is "I need". You already know चाहिए from Module 10, and the two overlap — मुझे पानी चाहिए and मुझे पानी की ज़रूरत है mean much the same, with the ज़रूरत version slightly more emphatic and more written. ज़रूरत is feminine and ends in a consonant, so nothing about its shape tells you that — flag it alongside उम्मीद and कोशिश. Note the की in that construction: the thing needed goes in the genitive before ज़रूरत, which is not what चाहिए does at all.

examples.note: The thing needed takes की before ज़रूरत.
The gift protest from Module 12 — you have already met this whole sentence.

examples.english: Let me know if you need anything.
examples.note: ज़रूरत पड़ना, for a need to arise. तो carrying the conditional.

common_error.why_en: ज़रूरत takes की on the thing needed. चाहिए does not, which is where the confusion comes from.

practice.explanation_en: A need or necessity — the noun that sits behind चाहिए.

game.question_en: A government form would use which word for ज़रूरत?
game.explanation_en: आवश्यकता is the Sanskrit-side equivalent used in official writing. माँग is a demand and कमी is a shortage.

summary.recap_en: Three feminine abstract nouns that all end in consonants and none of which look feminine — उम्मीद, कोशिश, ज़रूरत. All three sit inside constructions rather than standing alone: उम्मीद है कि, कोशिश करना, की ज़रूरत है.

learn.title_en: मुश्किल is both a noun and an adjective
learn.explanation_en: मुश्किल means difficult and also a difficulty, and Hindi uses the same word for both without changing it. ये काम मुश्किल है — this work is difficult. एक मुश्किल है — there's a difficulty. As a noun it is feminine, and as an adjective it does not inflect at all, because adjectives ending in a consonant never do. As a noun it is feminine and consonant-final, so flag it. The Sanskrit-side pair is कठिन, which you will meet in level 25.

examples.note: Adjective, and it does not agree with anything.
Noun, feminine, so गई.
मुश्किल से means "with difficulty", i.e. barely.

common_error.why_en: Adjectives ending in a consonant never take -आ, -ए or -ी. मुश्किल stays as it is.

practice.explanation_en: Literally "from difficulty" — it means only just.

game.question_en: Which word means difficult in a formal written register?
game.explanation_en: कठिन is the Sanskrit-side pair. सख़्त is strict or hard to the touch, and भारी is heavy.

learn.title_en: -आई turns an adjective into a noun
learn.explanation_en: सच is true; सच्चाई is truth. The suffix -आई builds abstract nouns from adjectives, and every noun it makes is feminine — which is why this one is not flagged. You have already met others without noticing: लंबाई length, गहराई depth, कमाई earnings, सफ़ाई cleaning. Once you have the suffix you can recognise a whole family of words you have never been taught.

examples.note: Feminine, so आती है.
ने, and बताई agreeing with feminine सच्चाई.

examples.hindi: इस कमरे की लंबाई कितनी है?
examples.read_as: is kamre kii lambaaii kitnii hai?
examples.english: What's the length of this room?
examples.note: Another -आई noun, also feminine.

common_error.why_en: Every -आई noun is feminine, without exception.

options: makes a verb from a noun
makes a feminine abstract noun from an adjective
practice.explanation_en: सच becomes सच्चाई, लंबा becomes लंबाई, गहरा becomes गहराई. All feminine.

game.question_en: Which word is closest to सच्चाई in a legal or official document?
game.explanation_en: सत्य is the Sanskrit-side word for truth. ईमान is faith or integrity, and यक़ीन is certainty.

learn.title_en: -ई builds abstract nouns too, and they are feminine as well
learn.explanation_en: आज़ाद is free; आज़ादी is freedom. The suffix -ई does the same job as -आई and produces feminine nouns just as reliably: ख़ुशी happiness, ग़रीबी poverty, दोस्ती friendship, बीमारी illness. Between -आई and -ई you can now recognise most Hindi abstract nouns on sight, and you can predict their gender without being told, which is unusual enough in this language to be worth noticing.

examples.note: Two -ई nouns in one sentence: आज़ादी and आसानी.
Feminine throughout — पूरी, दी, गई.

examples.english: Our friendship is an old one.
examples.note: दोस्ती, another -ई noun, also feminine.

practice.prompt_en: Which of these is NOT a feminine abstract noun in -ई?
practice.explanation_en: पानी ends in -ी but is masculine and is not derived from an adjective. The suffix rule only covers derived abstract nouns.

game.question_en: Which word would a formal history text use for आज़ादी?
game.explanation_en: स्वतंत्रता is the Sanskrit-side word. छूट is an exemption, अधिकार a right, and जीत a victory.

summary.recap_en: Two suffixes that build abstract nouns and always produce feminines: -आई (सच्चाई, लंबाई, गहराई) and -ई (आज़ादी, ख़ुशी, दोस्ती). Between them they cover most abstract nouns in Hindi, and they let you predict a gender for once. मुश्किल is both a noun and an adjective and never changes shape.

learn.explanation_en: भरोसा is trust, and the person you trust takes पर: मुझे उस पर भरोसा है, I trust him. Not को and not में — trust rests on somebody. It is masculine and ends in -आ, so the gender is predictable for once. The related यक़ीन means certainty rather than trust and takes the same पर, while विश्वास is the Sanskrit-side word and belongs to written and religious register.

examples.note: Dative on the truster, पर on the trusted.
Masculine, so गया. And the trust broke — nobody broke it.
भरोसा करना with मत, and इस oblique before पर.

common_error.why_en: The person trusted takes पर, not को.

practice.explanation_en: Trust rests on somebody: उस पर भरोसा.

game.question_en: Which word means trust in a religious or formal written context?
game.explanation_en: विश्वास is the Sanskrit-side word. यक़ीन is certainty rather than trust, and उम्मीद is hope.

learn.explanation_en: अनुभव covers experience as accumulated skill (उसे दस साल का अनुभव है) and experience as something that happened to you (यह एक नया अनुभव था). It is masculine and ends in a consonant, so it is flagged. This is a Sanskrit-derived word and it leans formal — a CV, a job advert or a news report will use it, and in casual speech people often say तजुर्बा instead, which is the Urdu-side equivalent and means exactly the same thing.

examples.hindi: उसे दस साल का अनुभव है।
examples.read_as: use das saal kaa anubhav hai.
examples.note: Dative on the person, and का agreeing with masculine अनुभव.
नया and था both masculine.

examples.hindi: अनुभव के आधार पर कहा जा सकता है।
examples.read_as: anubhav ke aadhaar par kahaa jaa saktaa hai.
examples.english: It can be said on the basis of experience.
examples.note: Formal register — this sentence would be odd in conversation.

common_error.wrong: उसे दस साल की अनुभव है
common_error.right: उसे दस साल का अनुभव है

practice.explanation_en: Both accumulated experience and a single experience.

game.question_en: A friend telling you a story would more likely use which word?
game.explanation_en: तजुर्बा is the Urdu-side equivalent and is what conversation prefers. अभ्यास is practice, ज्ञान is knowledge, and परीक्षा is a test.

tts_strings: उसे दस साल का अनुभव है।

learn.title_en: फ़ैसला — a decision, and a court's verdict
learn.explanation_en: फ़ैसला is a decision you make and also a verdict a court delivers, and news reports use it constantly in the second sense. It goes with करना — मैंने फ़ैसला किया, with किया masculine because फ़ैसला is. It also goes with लेना: फ़ैसला लेना is equally correct and slightly more deliberate. The Sanskrit-side word निर्णय means the same and is what a written judgement will say.

examples.note: करना with the लेना vector — decided, and settled.
का because फ़ैसला is masculine, and a verdict "comes".
आसान is a consonant-final adjective and does not inflect.

common_error.why_en: फ़ैसला is masculine, so करना agrees with it as किया.

practice.explanation_en: फ़ैसला covers both an everyday decision and a legal verdict.

game.question_en: A written judgement would use which word?
game.explanation_en: निर्णय is the Sanskrit-side word for a decision or judgement. राय is an opinion and सलाह is advice.

summary.recap_en: भरोसा takes पर — trust rests on somebody. अनुभव and फ़ैसला both have partners on the other side of the register: तजुर्बा for conversation, निर्णय for a written judgement. Neither pair is better than the other; they belong to different situations.

learn.title_en: ख़याल — a thought, and looking after someone
learn.explanation_en: ख़याल is a thought or an idea, and in ख़याल रखना it means care: बच्चों का ख़याल रखना is to look after the children. Those two senses are far apart in English and one word in Hindi, so context does all the work. It is also the polite way to disagree — मेरे ख़याल से, in my view — which is the same move as मेरे हिसाब से from Module 12. Masculine, consonant-final, flagged.

examples.hindi: मेरे ख़याल से ये ठीक नहीं है।
examples.read_as: mere ḳhayaal se ye ṭhiik nahiiṁ hai.
examples.english: In my view this isn't right.
examples.note: Disagreeing as an opinion rather than a correction.
The standard goodbye to someone you are fond of.

examples.english: A thought suddenly came to me.
examples.note: The thought comes; the person is not the subject.

common_error.why_en: ख़याल is masculine, and it is oblique before से, so मेरा goes to मेरे.

practice.explanation_en: ख़याल रखना is to look after, and it is one of the warmest ways to say goodbye.

game.question_en: Which word could replace ख़याल in मेरे ख़याल से?
game.explanation_en: मेरे विचार से is the Sanskrit-side equivalent and sounds more formal. सपना is a dream and इरादा an intention.

tts_strings: मेरे ख़याल से ये ठीक नहीं है।

learn.explanation_en: मक़सद is a purpose or an aim, and it is the word you reach for when asking what something is for: इसका मक़सद क्या है? It is masculine and consonant-final, so it is flagged. The Sanskrit-side pair is उद्देश्य, which is what a policy document or a school syllabus will say, and लक्ष्य is a target rather than a purpose — closer to a goal you are aiming at than a reason you are acting.

examples.note: इसका, masculine, agreeing with मक़सद.

examples.hindi: मेरा मक़सद किसी को दुख देना नहीं था।
examples.read_as: meraa maqsad kisii ko dukh denaa nahiiṁ thaa.
examples.english: It wasn't my intention to hurt anyone.
examples.note: A standard apology — and an infinitive as the complement.

examples.hindi: वो अपने मक़सद में कामयाब हुआ।
examples.read_as: vo apne maqsad meṁ kaamyaab huaa.
examples.note: मक़सद goes oblique to मक़सद before में — no visible change, but अपना moves to अपने.

common_error.why_en: मक़सद is masculine despite the consonant ending.

practice.explanation_en: The purpose or point of something.

game.question_en: A policy document would use which word for मक़सद?
game.explanation_en: उद्देश्य is the Sanskrit-side word. नतीजा is a result and तरीक़ा a method.

tts_strings: मेरा मक़सद किसी को दुख देना नहीं था।

learn.explanation_en: हालात means circumstances, and it is a plural — the singular is हाल, condition. It is an Arabic plural borrowed whole into Hindi, so you cannot make it plural again and you must give it a plural verb: हालात ठीक नहीं हैं, not है. Hindi has a handful of these borrowed plurals and they catch learners every time. It is masculine as well as plural, and consonant-final, so it is flagged twice over. News reports use हालात constantly for the general state of things.

examples.note: Plural verb, because हालात is already plural.

examples.hindi: हालात के हिसाब से फ़ैसला करेंगे।
examples.read_as: haalaat ke hisaab se faislaa kareṁge.
examples.english: We'll decide according to the circumstances.
examples.note: के हिसाब से from Module 12, with हालात oblique in front of it.
The singular हाल, in the everyday greeting.

common_error.why_en: हालात is a plural noun and takes a plural verb, even though it looks singular to an English eye.

practice.explanation_en: It is a borrowed Arabic plural of हाल, so it takes a plural verb.

game.question_en: Which word is closest to हालात in a formal report?
game.explanation_en: परिस्थिति is the Sanskrit-side word for circumstances. मामला is a matter or affair, and घटना an incident.

summary.recap_en: ख़याल covers a thought and looking after somebody, and मेरे ख़याल से is how you disagree politely. मक़सद is what something is for. And हालात is a borrowed Arabic plural — it takes a plural verb however singular it looks.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the first three words for what people are like.

learn.explanation_en: ईमान is integrity; ईमानदार is somebody who has it. The suffix -दार means "holding, possessing", and it builds a family of adjectives you will now recognise: समझदार sensible, ज़िम्मेदार responsible, दुकानदार shopkeeper, चौकीदार watchman. None of them inflects, because they all end in a consonant. That is a useful piece of stability — a whole class of personality adjectives with no agreement to get wrong.

examples.note: No agreement at all, because the adjective ends in a consonant.
Identical form for a feminine noun. Nothing changes.
Add -ई and you get the abstract noun, feminine as always.

common_error.why_en: ईमानदार is the adjective; ईमानदारी is the noun, honesty. The -ई suffix from level 2 does the same job here.

practice.explanation_en: ईमानदार, समझदार, ज़िम्मेदार, दुकानदार — all built the same way.

game.question_en: Which word describes someone who can be relied on to do their job properly?
game.explanation_en: ज़िम्मेदार is responsible. ईमानदार is specifically about honesty, मेहनती about effort, and समझदार about judgement.

learn.title_en: Adjectives in -ी do not agree either
learn.explanation_en: मेहनत is hard work; मेहनती is hardworking. This one ends in -ी and still does not inflect, which surprises learners who have learned that -ा adjectives change to -ी for feminine. The rule is about the ending you start from: only adjectives ending in -आ inflect. Everything else — मेहनती, ज़िद्दी, ग़रीबी nouns aside, ईमानदार, ख़ुश, तेज़ — stays exactly as it is, for every gender and number.

examples.note: Masculine, and मेहनती does not change.
Feminine, and मेहनती still does not change.
A set phrase — literally, hard work brings colour. मेहनत is feminine.

common_error.why_en: मेहनती is invariable. Trying to make a masculine form out of it produces a word that does not exist.

practice.prompt_en: Which adjectives inflect for gender in Hindi?
practice.explanation_en: बड़ा becomes बड़ी. But मेहनती, ईमानदार and तेज़ never change.

game.question_en: Which word praises the results rather than the effort?
game.explanation_en: कामयाब is successful — it judges the outcome. मेहनती judges only the work put in, which is the distinction being tested.

learn.title_en: ज़िद्दी — stubborn, and not always an insult
learn.explanation_en: ज़िद is insistence; ज़िद्दी is somebody who insists. Said of a child it is affectionate exasperation, said of an adult in an argument it is a complaint, and said of somebody who refused to give up it is close to praise. Tone carries all of that, and the word itself is neutral. Like मेहनती it ends in -ी and never inflects. Note ज़िद करना, to insist — the noun plus करना pattern again.

examples.note: Affectionate in most mouths.
ज़िद करना, to insist, with मत for the instruction.

examples.hindi: वो अपनी ज़िद पर अड़ी रही।
examples.read_as: vo apnii zid par aṛii rahii.
examples.note: ज़िद is feminine, so अपनी and अड़ी.

common_error.why_en: ज़िद्दी never changes, for any gender.

practice.explanation_en: The noun ज़िद plus करना — to be insistent about something.

game.question_en: Which word describes somebody who gives in easily?
game.explanation_en: लचीला is flexible — the opposite of ज़िद्दी. अड़ियल is a close synonym of ज़िद्दी, and सख़्त is strict.

summary.recap_en: Personality adjectives are mostly invariable: -दार words like ईमानदार and ज़िम्मेदार, and -ी words like मेहनती and ज़िद्दी. Only adjectives ending in -आ inflect. And ज़िद्दी shows how much of a Hindi word's meaning is carried by tone rather than by the word.
summary.next_up_en: Next: the first reading block — signs and notices, and reading rather than listening.
